A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VQMoE research despite the title change. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, fine-tuning, image-classification, robustness, and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds discrete-only training, clustering-comparator, segmentation, repeated-run, and large-model evaluations in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The core continuous/discrete architecture, training losses, and discrete-only fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds a training-free adaptation using pretrained OLMoE routers for codebook embeddings. The explicit modulo mapping in Section 3.2 elaborates hashing already contemplated in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds ADE20K semantic segmentation and six MTEB task categories, including clustering, reranking, semantic similarity, and summarization. Table 8 lists 18 task–dataset rows, although the accompanying text claims 19 datasets. The original language-modeling, text-classification, and image-classification coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against the clustering-based MoCLE method in Table 5 and pretrained OLMoE in Table 8. The parameter-robustness comparison also narrows: v2 Figure 3 retains only SMoE, whereas v1 Figure 2 additionally includes SMoE-Dropout, XMoE, and StableMoE. Comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 50K/100K-step and top-k controls for discrete-only training, segmentation evaluation using mean accuracy and mIoU, and training-free MTEB evaluation with a 16-layer, 7B-parameter model using 64 experts and top-k 8. These extend the evaluation design; they do not establish reruns or changed settings for the retained benchmark results.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a substantive test of whether discrete-only representations suffice when training from scratch, including model-scale and routing controls. Figure 2 adds convergence trajectories on WikiText-103 and lm1b. The earlier quantizer, codebook-size, loss-weight, consistency, and representation-collapse analyses are retained, while the parameter-robustness comparison is revised.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly reports means and standard deviations over three Text8 training runs for VQMoE, SMoE, XMoE, and StableMoE. The existing three-seed vision reporting and single-run ImageNet setting remain unchanged. v2 acknowledges that comprehensive repeated evaluations and formal significance testing were not performed.

E6.justification: The individual scores in Tables 1–3 are retained, but v2 adds aggregate columns, convergence curves, and Tables 4–8. New findings include discrete-only VQMoE underperforming large SMoE at top-k 1 (1.14 versus 1.12 BPC), segmentation scores of 23.4 mean accuracy and 16.6 mIoU, and MTEB averages of 56.6 versus OLMoE’s 54.1. The robustness plots also change dataset-to-value associations, apparently exchanging the Enwik8 and Text8 series.

T1.justification: The router definitions and principal theorem/proposition statements are retained despite relocation and renumbering. However, the optimal-selection proof changes from expert-output comparisons and sums over cluster–expert pairs to explicit loss comparisons between experts. The Jacobian derivation is also reworked in Appendix A.1.1; these are mathematical revisions, not merely formatting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about discrete expert selection, routing inconsistency, representation collapse, language/vision effectiveness, and the 28% benefit. Despite softer wording in the contribution bullets, the introduction still claims optimal expert selection and solving collapse by design. The additional experiments mainly support existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds the important qualification that discrete-only training works at small scale but falls below SMoE at larger scale, and explains VQ’s advantage over MoCLE through adaptable cluster representations. It explicitly defines robustness as performance under parameter reduction. Section 5.3 also replaces the claimed gain exceeding 5% over the second-best method with an average gain exceeding 2.5% over SMoE.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the modulo code-to-expert mapping, task-loss examples, a stated 90:5:5 split, the half-width robustness configuration, and 16 experts in the pretraining settings table. These primarily expand documentation. The existing optimizer, learning rates, training budgets, two-H100 hardware disclosure, and underlying implementation link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting MoCLE, OLMoE, MTEB, Segmenter, ADE20K, and implementation explanations, including a new substantive comparison with clustering-based routing. The related-work section and the claimed novelty of learning discrete representations for SMoE remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanations are substantially rewritten, experimental-setting descriptions are consolidated, and contributions become a bullet list. Router definitions move into the main theory section, while the appendices are reorganized under a unified hierarchy with a new experimental-results section. The title also changes.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is completely redrawn; convergence plots and five result tables are added; Tables 1–2 gain average columns; and the robustness plots change legends, markers, and displayed comparisons. The two earlier representation-dynamics figures are merged into v2 Figure 5. Typography, table highlighting, and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The discrete-only scaling ablation, three-run Text8 results, and clearer routing documentation make the method’s limitations and reliability more assessable than in v1. These gains are tempered by new reporting errors: Table 2 gives StableMoE an average of 73.89 although its displayed scores average about 73.14, and the robustness panels apparently exchange dataset series. The added evidence supports a limited overall improvement, rather than resolving the paper’s central theoretical and reporting weaknesses.
